title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). Pi = pi_{0,3}^ is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,oo}. The symmetric group S_3 acts on it through rho, of order 3 (cyclic permutation of 0,1,oo), and the involution sigma_oo (fixing oo, i.e. z -> 1-z). M_{0,3}^{!~} is a group of automorphisms u of the semidirect product Pi x| S_3 that are compatible with this structure. It is an extension of N_{0,3}^{!~} by Pi, and N_{0,3}^{!~} is Grothendieck's own version of what Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara called GT^.

Cocycle description (pp. 210-211).
- Such a u is given by u(sigma_oo) = h sigma_oo and u(rho) = g rho.
- The 1-cocycle conditions are g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1 and h sigma_oo(h) = 1.
- The compatibility condition is g = h l_1^nu.
- These amount to Drinfeld's hexagon and 2-cycle relations for a pair (lambda, f) in GT^.
- Grothendieck writes the cocycles as coboundaries: g = alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} and h = beta sigma_oo(beta)^{-1}. Then u(rho) = int(alpha) rho and u(sigma_oo) = int(beta) sigma_oo.
- The compatibility condition becomes the 'relation des lacets' (97): alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} = (beta sigma_oo(beta)^{-1}) l_1^nu, with nu in Z^ 'convenable'.

Passage to N (this page).
- The subgroup M^{!~}[0] corresponds to the tangential base point at 0. It meets Pi in L_0 = <l_0> ~ Z^, the inertia at 0.
- Since M^{!~}[0]/L_0 ~ N^{!~}, Grothendieck obtains his 'Cor. Main': N_{0,3}^{!~} is in canonical bijection with the set of pairs (alpha, beta) in Pi^ x Pi^ satisfying the loop relation, modulo (alpha, beta) ~ (l_0^n alpha, l_0^n beta).
- The group law is given by the cocycle formulas (125): g'' = u'(g) g', h'' = u'(h) h', alpha'' = u'(alpha) alpha', beta'' = u'(beta) beta'.
- Check: u'u(rho) = u'(int(alpha) rho) = int(u'(alpha) alpha') rho, which is consistent.

Second part: sections attached to algebraic points.
- For every algebraic point q of P^1 minus {0,1,oo}, with field k_q, a rational point should give a section of 1 -> Pi -> pi_1 -> Gal. This is the arithmetic side of the section-conjecture picture.
- Grothendieck proposes that this section extends to a 'partial section' K_q : M^{!~}(q) -> M^{!~} of the extension of N^{!~} by Pi. Here M^{!~}(q) is a hypothetical subgroup, 'to be determined', playing the role of the stabilizer Gamma_Q(q).
- The earlier cases 1 and 2 are q = 1/2 and q = -j. These are the fixed points of sigma_oo and of rho, i.e. the 2-cycle and hexagon relations. For q = 1/2 the stabilizer is all of Gamma_Q; for q = -j it is the index-2 kernel of eps_2 o chi.
- Transporting by S_3 gives K_2 and K_{-1} from K_{1/2}. The tangential base point at 0 corresponds to M[0].
- The aim is to extend these GT-level splittings from the S_3-special points to arbitrary algebraic points.
errors: On p.210, (118) gives u(sigma_oo) = int(alpha) sigma_oo and u(rho) = int(beta) rho. But with g = alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} one gets g rho = int(alpha) rho, so alpha belongs with rho and beta with sigma_oo. Either the roles are swapped in (118) or the transcription is wrong.

alpha and beta are determined only up to right multiplication by the centralizers of rho and sigma_oo in Pi x| S_3. The bijection in 'Cor. Main' therefore needs either a normalization of alpha and beta, or the claim that this ambiguity is exactly the L_0 action. As written, this is not justified on the page.

That every cocycle g (g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1) is a coboundary alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} is a nontrivial H^1(Z/3, Pi) statement. Cocycles may differ by conjugacy class of the finite subgroup, which is where the fixed points -j and -j^2 enter. The page implicitly assumes it is a coboundary.

ideas.what: Description of the GT-type group N_{0,3} as S_3-equivariant automorphisms of pi_{0,3}^ x| S_3, via cocycles (g,h) satisfying the 3-cycle, 2-cycle and loop relations
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck-Teichmüller group GT^ (Drinfeld's hexagon and 2-cycle relations)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the 'tour de Teichmüller' and to Gal acting on the 0- and 1-dimensional levels; no explicit presentation

ideas.what: Re-parametrizing GT elements by pairs (alpha, beta) with g = alpha rho(alpha)^{-1}, modulo l_0^n tied to the tangential base point at 0 (the 'relation des lacets')
ideas.modern_name: coboundary/torsor description of GT^; tangential base point normalization

ideas.what: Group law given by the cocycle formulas g'' = u'(g) g', etc.
ideas.modern_name: Composition law of GT^ (Drinfeld's multiplication law)

ideas.what: For each algebraic point q of M_{0,3}, a partial splitting K_q of M_{0,3}^{!~} -> N_{0,3}^{!~} over a hypothetical stabilizer subgroup M(q), extending the Galois section of the rational point; special cases q = 1/2 and q = -j matching the 2-cycle and hexagon relations
ideas.modern_name: lifting Galois sections of rational/algebraic points to GT^; GT analogue of the section conjecture / decomposition groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: no clear attribution; related themes in Nakamura, Hoshi-Minamide-Mochizuki, Minamide-Nakamura

missed.claim: Grothendieck poses the problem of defining, for every algebraic point q of P^1 minus {0,1,oo}, a subgroup M_{0,3}(q) of the GT-type group extending the Galois stabilizer Gamma_Q(q), together with a partial splitting K_q. This would extend the rational-point section to GT^. He has done this only for the S_3-special points 1/2 and -j.
missed.quote: pour tout point algébrique q ∈ M_{0,3}(C) ... on obtient ... une section partielle K_q : M_{0,3}^{!~}(q) → M_{0,3}^{!~}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether GT^ (or subgroups of it) acts compatibly on sections attached to non-special algebraic points is an open-ended question. It touches the 'GT = Gal_Q?' problem and the section conjecture for the tripod. It is not, to my knowledge, systematically treated in the literature.

missed.claim: Drinfeld's 2-cycle and hexagon relations are interpreted as the existence of GT-level splittings at the S_3-fixed points 1/2 and -j, with stabilizers Gamma_Q and ker(eps_2 o chi) respectively. These are viewed as the first instances of a general 'decomposition group at a point' theory for GT.
missed.quote: L'analyse des cas 1° et 2° ci-dessus revenait en fait à la détermination de tels scindages, pour q=1/2 et pour q=-j
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives a geometric/arithmetic interpretation of the defining relations of GT^ in terms of sections at special points. Known informally, but phrased here as a programme toward arbitrary points.

deep.surprise_reason: Most of the page is Grothendieck's private derivation of a GT^-type presentation, a decade before Drinfeld; this is known in outline from the Longue Marche material. The proposal to attach GT-level partial splittings to arbitrary algebraic points, generalizing the q = 1/2 and q = -j cases, is a speculative, unfinished program that seems not to have been pursued explicitly.
transcription_corrections: 'relation de Contou[?] (97)' is likely 'relation des lacets (97)'; the previous page calls (97) 'la sempiternelle relation des lacets'.
In the relation, 'overline{tau}_0(beta)' should probably read sigma_oo(beta), consistent with p.210.
'π_{0,3}^{~∧}' for alpha is presumably the same group pi_{0,3}^ (or a variant with tilde) as for beta.
In the inserted line, 'M_{0,3}^{!~}(0)' should probably be M_{0,3}^{!~}[0].
(126) margin: 'ou seulement un sous-anneau[?]' is uncertain; it may refer to q being algebraic over Q with field k_q = Q(q).
